clue.text: Old lady cheers a couple of home guards for support

indicators.note: guards stand on either side of what they protect, so one piece is flanked by the others

blocks.note: one's old lady is one's mother, informally ma
home is IN, as in staying in; a couple means two of them
ta is British informal thanks, often used like cheers

explanation.surface: An elderly woman toasts a pair of Home Guard soldiers for backing her.
explanation.walkthrough: The two INs sit either side of TA, so the pair guards it; the Home Guard was Britain's wartime volunteer militia.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a family or a structure is to support it, keeping it going or holding it up.

clue.text: Isolated feature in the main is secure

blocks.note: taken as written
to secure a job or a deal is to land it

explanation.surface: A lone spot out in the open sea is safe ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the old poetic name for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land standing alone, surrounded by ocean water on every side.

clue.text: Reward school seen differently on coming first

indicators.note: seen differently means the letters are rearranged into another order

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, and coming first puts it at the front
a comp is a British comprehensive, a state secondary school
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A school is rewarded once it is viewed in a new light by coming top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming first' tells you to put the word for on at the front, not that anything wins.
explanation.definitionFit: A recompense is payment or compensation given in return for effort, service or loss.

clue.text: Half-cut banter in bar

indicators.note: cut in half means only one half of the word survives, the other is lopped off

blocks.note: raillery is good-humoured teasing banter

explanation.surface: Tipsy joking in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, which fits the bar, but here it halves the eight-letter word for banter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a horizontal bar, such as a towel rail or a handrail on stairs.

clue.text: Massage a drop of this into men?

definitions.text: Massage a drop of this into men?

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of this is used
massaging kneads and works things around, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of this
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to rub a little of this cream into the men.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: rubbing a little into the skin is exactly what you do with the product.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a greasy medicinal preparation that you massage into the skin.

clue.text: Artist's concealing this woman's skin problems

indicators.note: something concealing another hides it within itself

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist, plus the 's
the pronoun for this woman

explanation.surface: A painter is covering up a woman's skin complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashes are patches of red, irritated or spotty skin, a common type of complaint.

clue.text: Recited key passage in theatre?

indicators.note: something recited is spoken out, so we go by its sound and not its spelling

blocks.note: a key or cay is a small low island, an isle

explanation.surface: An actor speaking an important speech on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key passage' reads as a crucial bit of a script, but key is a low island and passage is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The aisle is the walkway between rows of seats in a theatre or church.

clue.text: Staying power enlivens without energy returning

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter standing for energy is taken away
returning means going back, so what is left is read from the end

blocks.note: to enliven something is to animate it

explanation.surface: Endurance perks you up, unless you run out of energy on the way back.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the physical or mental endurance to keep going over a long effort.

clue.text: Bank raising standing order urgently

blocks.note: SO is the abbreviation for a standing order, a regular bank payment; raising lifts it to the top of this down entry
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A bank pushing up its regular payment instructions as a matter of urgency.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, raising one piece puts it on top, so the abbreviation comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorely means badly or greatly, as in sorely needed, describing a pressing need.

clue.text: Approved of batting average contributing to batsman's score

indicators.note: contributing to suggests being put into something, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a cricket side batting is said to be in
a four is a boundary scored by a batsman in cricket
AV is the standard abbreviation for average

explanation.surface: A cricket report praising a player whose average helped the score.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a four is scored when the ball crosses the boundary after bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in favour means supported or liked, the state of having approval from people.

clue.text: Fruit left one with irritating sensation inside

indicators.note: inside places one thing between the parts of another

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
I is the Roman numeral one
an itch is an irritating sensation on the skin

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit left a person with a tickle in the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, more often spelt lychee, is a small Chinese fruit with sweet white flesh.

clue.text: Unmarried woman losing heart in Spanish city

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letters of the word drop out

blocks.note: the capital of Spain

explanation.surface: A single woman becoming downhearted while living in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid, as in old maid, is a traditional word for a girl or a woman not yet wed.

clue.text: He spoilt my irrational belief

indicators.note: irrational means lacking order or logic, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a man ruined their unreasonable conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Polytheism is the religious creed that holds there are many gods rather than one.

clue.text: Broadcast right artists on radio

indicators.note: broadcast once meant scattering seed widely, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Performers being aired on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link to radio but its letters are in the mix; the definition is just radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor is a small portable radio set, named after the electronic component inside it.

clue.text: Flower exhibited in phenomenal retrospective

indicators.note: exhibited in means shown inside the next word, sitting among its letters
retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: A bloom on show in an outstanding gallery retrospective.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a garden plant of the buttercup family with bright cup-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Dancing femme fatale that did harm essentially

definitions.text: Dancing femme fatale that did harm essentially

indicators.note: the essence of each word is its core, so only the central letters are kept
dancing letters move about and settle into a fresh order

blocks.note: the central letter of this five-letter word
the central pair of this six-letter word
the central pair
the central letter
the central pair

explanation.surface: A seductive dancer who caused real damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word after 'Dancing' gives up its middle; the whole clue then describes the woman, so it is wordplay and definition at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Mata Hari was a Dutch exotic dancer executed by France in 1917 as a German spy.

clue.text: Musical work uses computers in opening section

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: the opening section of a document is often labelled Part A
IT, information technology, covers computers

explanation.surface: A composition that employs computers at its start.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a Baroque instrumental suite, such as those Bach wrote for solo violin.

clue.text: Errant fools disheartened about move

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letters of the word go
about suggests turning things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
only the outside letters remain once the middle goes

explanation.surface: Wayward idiots feeling glum over a relocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Errant' looks like an anagram signal but is the fodder; 'about' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer is to shift something from one place, job or owner to another.

clue.text: Official list of people in Central and South America

blocks.note: CEN is an abbreviation for central
S is the compass abbreviation
the United States, commonly called America

explanation.surface: A register of the population of Latin America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central and South America' reads as one region, but it splits into three abbreviations; 'and' merely joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is the official count and record of a country's population taken by government.

clue.text: Reduced length spoiled new edition of Sense and Sensibility

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its last letter
something spoiled has been messed up, so those letters are scrambled
a new edition rearranges the material, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the word with its final letter cut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shortened, botched reissue of Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel's title is split: 'Sense' is fodder and 'Sensibility' is the definition, with 'and' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensibility means delicate feeling and tenderness, close to softness of manner and kindly mildness.

clue.text: Satisfy speculators' expectations initially when returning high value

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words before it
returning means coming back, so the whole is read in the other direction

blocks.note: to satisfy a demand is to meet it
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Investors' forecasts are met when a pricey asset bounces back.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is the high regard or respect in which someone or something is held.

clue.text: One may be in a rut and decline over time

definitions.text: One may be in a rut

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: to decline or droop is to sag
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a routine who goes downhill as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: A rut is the deer's mating season, not a groove of routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, and male deer compete for mates during the autumn rut.

clue.text: What has two musical notes separating in this way?

definitions.text: What has two musical notes separating in this way?

indicators.note: things separating a word sit between its letters and push them apart

blocks.note: so means in this way
te and re are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A riddle about a thing that splits music into two parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a stereo plays sound split between two channels.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo sound is recorded and played through two separate channels, left and right.

clue.text: Carves piece of sweet chestnut

indicators.note: a piece of something is a part of it, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone whittles a bit of sweet chestnut wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface, engraving it with a tool or acid.

clue.text: Good man joining resistance inspires independence movement

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so a letter is drawn inside

blocks.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A decent man joins the resistance and fires up a freedom campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independence movement' reads as a political campaign; movement is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a commotion or bustle, a slight movement such as a stir in the crowd.

clue.text: American poet almost captures state of uncertainty

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
to capture is to hold within, so the other piece goes inside

blocks.note: Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, minus his last letter
US for the United States

explanation.surface: A US poet nearly sums up a mood of doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American poet' suggests one American writer, but the poet is the English Spenser and 'American' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious uncertainty felt while waiting for something to be decided or revealed.

clue.text: What judges do to avoid beginning what eavesdropper does

indicators.note: avoiding the beginning means the opening letter is skipped

blocks.note: British judges traditionally wear wigs in court

explanation.surface: Judges keeping clear of the start of what a snooper gets up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What judges do' suggests hear cases, but the answer is about their headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for eavesdropping, listening in secretly to a private talk.

clue.text: Honours European owning large corporation?

blocks.note: an OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A decorated European businessman who owns a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is old British slang for a pot belly, so owning a large one means being very fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means grossly overweight, carrying a big paunch or protruding stomach.
